author: Codex documentation author; corrections by DOC-029 source-review author agent (operator-lifecycle)

prerequisites: The populated installation upgraded to 3fa407e3 in openlaw-docs-41255c61-lc-upgrade, with known Version hashes, a saved encrypted relay, and retained keys copied to a private secret store.
A separate fresh clone at 3fa407e3 for the target project openlaw-docs-41255c61-lc-restore on 127.0.0.1:23332, with its own volumes.
scenarios.expected: Records and permissions work, file hashes match, and required encrypted configuration is usable with the retained key. Missing/wrong keys or missing files are detected; a backup archive alone never counts as a successful restore.
scenarios.actual: Took the backup exactly as written: a fresh mode-700 directory, app and worker stopped with Postgres running, pg_dump custom format, the file volume archived through the app service, app-source.txt and images.json recorded (all exit 0), pg_restore --list gave 684 entries and tar listed 5 files, and SHA256SUMS was written. Step 5 restarted the services; readiness, a Contract read and a Version hash passed, and the copy in a separate retained directory passed sha256sum --check. The target was prepared from the recorded source with the retained AUTH_SECRET and OPENLAW_SECRET_KEY and no first-run setup. The hashes passed on the target, the database had zero tables and the file volume zero entries, pg_restore --exit-on-error --no-owner --no-privileges exited 0, and the archive filled the volume with 5 files. The target came up ready. The Administrator and the Legal Team Member signed in through the browser. Contracts, the Matter, the Entity and Field values matched the inventory, and all four original and later Version downloads matched their SHA-256. The Legal Team Member was refused the Confidential Contract and its Document. The Business User (former Contributor) kept portal reach on its member Contract only. A new PDF reached text ready, and a test email through the restored relay reached the controlled recipient. Negative checks: a valid-length wrong OPENLAW_SECRET_KEY kept Contracts readable, logged 'No configured key opens these stored credentials: smtp_url (1)', showed email as unset and refused the test send with 'SMTP is not configured — save a relay first.', and nothing was delivered. The retained key and a recreate restored delivery. Removing one stored blob left the Document listed while its download returned HTTP 500; extracting the retained archive again restored both Version hashes. With OPENLAW_SECRET_KEY removed, docker compose config --quiet and up both refused.

limitations: Independent agent walkthrough by a different agent from the author and the source reviewer; not a human operator study and not feature-owner approval.
The upgrade ran between two development revisions (d1d098ba to 3fa407e3), not between published releases.

Host Docker address pools were exhausted by other projects, so the walkthrough pre-created each project's two Compose networks with explicit subnets and Compose labels. The Compose files, services and network names were the articles' own.
The controlled relay was an owned Mailpit reachable as lc-mail on every project network, so the restored and recovered targets reached a controlled recipient under the relay name saved on the source.
Only the bundled Postgres and the local file volume were backed up and restored. Object-store snapshot tooling was not exercised.
Docker Compose 5.5.1 labels each built image with its project, so the same source has a different image ID in each project; build steps came from the build cache.
Provider guides and real provider checks C42/C43 stay blocked and are not waived. No human proofreading is recorded.
No account had two-factor authentication enrolled, so the 'Existing two-factor authentication no longer works' row was not exercised. The 'Import stopped partway through' row was not induced.

The pre-upgrade backup was also restored onto the starting build as part of V-C46 (see evidence/upgrade.json); that run used the HTTP sign-in API because the starting build's web client did not load in headless Chromium.

Walkthrough-r1.json keeps four failed restore-negative steps from a reviewer-script error (an async helper read as a plain result). They were fixed and all four passed on rerun; the dispositions are in the log.

compatibilityReview.summary: Inspected the 3fa407e3..57e77e38 app diff (SMTP discrete fields and storage format, public sign-in branding, logo limit, welcome URL steps, BASE_URL wording) and found no change to any backup, restore or verification statement. Replayed the round 1 V-C47 script on 57e77e38 in disposable Compose projects: backup, restore into an empty target, role and Confidential checks, Version hashes, relay test email, and the wrong-key, missing-blob and missing-key negatives all passed (45 of 45 steps).
